sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and runtime setting
sections.what: Loads the response helper and the anchor service, and tells the framework to run this file on the Node.js server runtime.
sections.why: Likely reason: the anchor service needs server features that are not available in the lighter runtime.

sections.name: GET
sections.title: Public anchor check handler
sections.what: Handles a GET request for one anchor id. It returns the verification details when found, and a not-found error otherwise.
sections.why: Lets the public check an anchor without signing in. Likely reason: verification must be open so outside parties can confirm results.
sections.watch_out: The first parameter is unused, and the anchor id must arrive through the route parameters in the shape the framework provides.

summary: A public web address that checks whether a saved anchor still matches a fresh recalculation of its original verification result.
purpose: Lets anyone who has an anchor id confirm that the sealed record has not changed.
why: Likely reason: a public check lets outside parties confirm that a signed result was not altered.
how: Reads the anchor id from the web address, asks the anchor service to verify it, returns the details if found, or returns a not-found message if the anchor does not exist.
inputs: The anchor id in the web address. The request body is ignored.
outputs: JSON with a data field holding the verification details, or a 404 response with the code NOT_FOUND.
risks: The route is public, so anything the verification returns is visible to anyone who knows the id. Errors thrown by the service are not caught here.
debug: Start with the verifyAnchor function in the anchor service. A 404 means no anchor exists with that id. Compare the response shape with the expectations in the anchor test file.
